title: API evolution checklist: graceful fallbacks and migration plan for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: As we introduce vNext behavior for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs, we need a pragmatic, low-risk migration path for customers. This ticket is the product-facing checklist and high-level coordination doc for flag-driven rollouts, migration guidance, and the backward-compatibility test suites engineers will run. Goals: (1) avoid breaking production clients, (2) provide clear opt-in/opt-out flags and SDK guidance, (3) bake automated regression checks into CI/canary, (4) provide written migration guides and example code for common edge cases (long-chunk streaming, partial tool-call handoffs, schema versioning for structured outputs).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A behavior-flag gate (legacy_behavior=true/false) exists in API gateway and SDKs to toggle vNext behavior per-API-key
A2: Backward-compat test harness runs nightly and verifies >=95% parity for existing production prompt set (baseline corpus) when legacy flag is enabled
A3: Migration guide published to Confluence with code samples for Node/Python/Go and a changelog section listing breaking and non-breaking differences
A4: SDK releases include opt-in fallbacks and clear deprecation warnings in logs; rollout plan for flag removal documented
A5: Canary rollout for vNext streaming enabled with automatic rollback on latency/regression thresholds defined (SLO deviations >10% or quality regression >5%)
implementation_notes: Flag model: introduce 'behavior.vnext' boolean on requests and API keys. Default remains false for now. Ensure API gateway honors flag precedence: request header > API key config > org default.

Streaming changes: chunk framing will change for vNext to include 'chunk_id' and optional 'meta.fragmented=true' for very long responses. Provide server-side compatibility adapter that emits legacy framing when legacy flag is set.

Tool/function calling: new signature adds 'call_context' with deterministic idempotency token. When legacy flag is set, runtime should map new call_context to old callback style and preserve original payload keys.

Structured outputs: introduce lightweight schema versioning field (schema_v). SDKs will ship validators that accept schema_v=1 (legacy) and schema_v=2 (new). Servers will include a fallback mapping layer for common misshapes (missing fields, null vs empty-string).
Telemetry: add 'migration_flag', 'schema_v', and 'toolcall_mode' dimensions to logs and tracing. Create dashboard panels for error_rate, latency_p50/p95, and token_cost delta between modes.

Testing: add unit+integration suites that replay recorded sessions from production (anonymized) under both flags and diff outputs. Include golden-file comparisons with tolerances for nondeterministic tokens.
qa_plan: Create a canonical prompt corpus (1000 prompts) representing streaming, tool-call, and structured-output usage in customer workloads
Run nightly comparator that checks for changes in: 1) end-to-end success (tool-call executed + expected output), 2) structured schema conformance, 3) streaming chunk ordering and reassembly
Add randomized fuzz tests for partial chunk loss and verify legacy adapter recovers gracefully
Define quality alerting rule: if automated eval shows >5% drop in expected structured fields across corpus, trigger rollback and investigation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dev: Implement server-side adapters behind feature flag; SDKs include opt-in flag for developers (internal dev users) - target 2 weeks
Phase 1 - Alpha: Opt-in via API key whitelist for internal partners; run comparison tests and collect telemetry - 1 sprint
Phase 2 - Canary: Select customer subset (~1% of traffic) with non-critical routes. Monitor SLOs and eval metrics; automated rollback thresholds applied - 2 sprints
Phase 3 - Early Access: Publish migration guide, expand whitelist to public signups, SDK docs and example apps updated
Phase 4 - General Availability: Flip default to vNext for new keys; legacy flag still supported for a defined deprecation window (6 months), during which we offer assisted migrations
Phase 5 - Removal: Announce removal at T-90/30/7 days, final telemetry validation, and decommission legacy adapter after agreed cutoff
